source_text: ὅτι μακρὰν ἀπὸ σοῦ ὁ τόπος ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ, ὅτι εὐλογήσει σε Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, καὶ ἀποδώσῃ αὐτὰ ἀργυρίου, καὶ λήψῃ τὸ ἀργύριον ἐν ταῖς χερσί σου, καὶ πορεύσῃ εἰς τὸν τόπον ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, αὐτὸν ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ, καὶ δώσεις ἀργύριον ἐπὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν ἐπιθυμῇ ἡ ψυχή σου, ἐπὶ βουσὶν ἢ ἐπὶ προβάτοις, ἢ ἐπ' οἴνῳ ἢ ἐπὶ σίκερα, ἢ ἐπὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν ἐπιθυμῇ ἡ ψυχή σου, καὶ φάγῃ ἐκεῖ ἐναντίον Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ σου, καὶ εὐφρανθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου, καὶ ὁ Λευίτης ὁ ἐν ταῖς πόλεσί σου, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτῷ μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος μετὰ σοῦ.» Ὁρᾷς τοῦ νόμου τὸ εὐτεχνὲς, καταψιλοῦντος τὸ ἄναντες, καὶ βάσιμα τὰ δυσπόρευτα τιθέντος εὖ μάλα, κατευμαρίζοντος δὲ καὶ τὰ λίαν δυσχερῆ; καὶ τοῦτο, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ, τὸ διὰ τῆς τοῦ προφήτου φωνῆς· «Ὁδὸς εὐσεβῶν εὐθεῖα ἐγένετο, καὶ παρεσκευασμένη ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν εὐσεβῶν.» Ἐπιτήρει δὲ ὅτι πανταχῆ τε καὶ ἀναγκαίως ὁ Λευίτης παραλαμβάνεται, καταδεικνύντος ἡμῖν ἐναργῶς τοῦ νόμου, ὡς οὐκ ἂν πρόσοιτο θυσίαν ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς ἐξ ἀνιέρου χειρὸς, καὶ ἀπᾴδοντος τοῦ νόμου προσκεκομισμένην. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἐκτετίμηται δὴ οὖν εἰσάπαν τὸ Λευιτικόν. {ΚΥΡ.} Παντάπασι μὲν οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε· Χριστοῦ γὰρ τύπος, καὶ ἐκμαγεῖον ὁ ἱερεύς· ὠνόμασται γὰρ μεσίτης Θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων, ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, ἀπόστολός τε καὶ ἀρχιερεὺς τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς Γραφὰς, ὃς οὐ δι' αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων ἐφάπαξ, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος. Καὶ μιᾷ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Ἄθρει δὲ, εἴ σοι δοκεῖ, καὶ καθ' ἕτερον τρόπον, τῇ δόξῃ Χριστοῦ στεφανούμενον τὸν ἱερουργόν· διαῤῥήδην γὰρ ἡμῖν ἀνακεκραγότος αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγοντος· «Οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκε τῷ Υἱῷ, ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν Υἱὸν, καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν Πατέρα·» καὶ μὴν δι' ἁγίου φωνῆς· «Εἷς ἐστιν ὁ νομοθέτης καὶ κριτὴς,» παρά γε τοῖς ἱεροῖς κείμενον Γράμμασιν, ἀναμέλποντος δὲ καὶ τοῦ θεσπεσίου Δαβὶδ, ὅτι «Θεὸς κριτής ἐστι.» Τὸ ἐπὶ τῷδε λαμπρὸν ἀξίωμα, τοῖς ἐξ αἵματος ἱεροῦ προσνέμων ὁ νομοθέτης, ὧδέ πή φησιν ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ· «Ἐὰν δὲ ἀδυνατήσῃ ἀπὸ σοῦ ῥῆμα ἐν κρίσει ἀναμέσον αἷμα αἵματος, καὶ ἀναμέσον κρίσις κρίσεως, καὶ ἀναμέσον ἁφὴ ἁφῆς, καὶ ἀναμέσον ἀντιλογία ἀντιλογίας, ῥήματα κρίσεως ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀναβήσῃ εἰς τὸν τόπον, ὃν ἂν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἐλεύσῃ πρὸς τοὺς ἱερεῖς τοὺς Λευίτας καὶ πρὸς τὸν κριτὴν ὃς ἂν γένηται ἐν ταῖς ἡ μέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ ἐκζητήσαντες ἀναγγελοῦσί σοι τὴν κρίσιν, καὶ ποιήσεις κατὰ τὸ πρᾶγμα ὃ ἂν ἀναγγείλωσί σοι ἐκ τοῦ τόπου οὗ ἐὰν ἐκλέξηται Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, καὶ φυλάξῃ ποιῆσαι πάντα ὅσα ἂν νομοθετηθῇ σοι. Κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ κατὰ τὴν κρίσιν ἢν ἂν εἴπωσί σοι, ποιήσεις. Οὐκ ἐκκλινεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ ῥήματος οὗ ἐὰν ἀναγγείλωσί σοι δεξιὰ οὐδὲ ἀριστερὰ, καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἐὰν ποιήσῃ
pass_a_gloss: [Deut 14:24b–27 LXX:] …because far from you the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called on there, because the Lord your God will bless you, and you will give them back for silver (= sell), take the silver in your hands, go to the place…, and give the silver for all your soul desires, on oxen or sheep, wine or strong drink, or all your soul desires, and eat there before the Lord, and rejoice, you and your house, and the Levite in your cities, because he has no portion nor lot with you. || You see the skilfulness of the law, stripping bare / levelling the uphill, and setting the hard to travel as passable very well, and making easy the very difficult. And this I think is the thing through the prophet's voice: the way of the godly became straight, and prepared the way of the godly. || Observe that everywhere and necessarily the Levite is taken along, the law showing plainly that the God of all would not accept a sacrifice from an unholy hand and brought discordant with the law. || PALL.: The Levitical then has been honored out altogether. || CYR.: Altogether so, O Palladius; for a type and impression of Christ the priest; for the Emmanuel has been named mediator of God and humans, apostle and high priest of our confession according to the Scriptures, who not through blood of goats and calves but through his own blood entered into the Holy of holies once for all, having found eternal redemption. And by one offering he has perfected for perpetuity those being sanctified. || Look, if it seems good, in another way too, the priest officiant crowned with Christ's glory: he having expressly cried out: 'the Father judges no one, but all judgment he has given to the Son, that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father'; and through a saint's voice 'one is the lawgiver and judge' lying in the sacred Letters; and divine David singing that 'God is judge'. The bright dignity on this, the lawgiver assigning to those of sacred blood, says thus somewhere in Deuteronomy: [Deut 17:8–12a LXX: if a word in judgment is impossible from you, between blood and blood, judgment and judgment, stroke and stroke, dispute and dispute, words of judgment in your cities, rising you will go up to the place the Lord your God chooses there, come to the priests the Levites and to the judge who is in those days, and having sought out they will announce the judgment; you will do according to the matter they announce from the place…, and keep to do all that is legislated for you; according to the law and the judgment they say you will do; you will not turn aside from the word they announce, right nor left; and the man who does…]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …because the place which the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called upon there is far from you, because the Lord your God will bless you, then you shall sell them for silver, and take the silver in your hands, and go to the place which the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called upon there. And you shall spend the silver on whatever your soul desires, on oxen or on sheep, on wine or on strong drink, or on whatever your soul desires; and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your household, and the Levite who is in your cities, because he has no portion or inheritance with you.’ (Deuteronomy 14:22–27) Do you see the skill of the law? It levels the steep climb, makes rough roads quite passable, and eases even what is very hard. And this, I think, is what was said through the voice of the prophet: ‘The way of the godly has become straight, and the way of the godly is made ready.’ (Isaiah 26:7) Notice too that the Levite is brought in everywhere and of necessity, since the law shows us plainly that the God of all would not accept a sacrifice offered by an unconsecrated hand, in a way that is at odds with the law.
Palladius: So the Levitical order has been held in the highest honor.

Cyril: Entirely so, Palladius. For the priest is a type and an imprint of Christ. Emmanuel has been named the Mediator between God and humans (1 Timothy 2:5), and the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, according to the Scriptures (Hebrews 3:1); he entered once for all into the Holy of Holies, not through the blood of goats and calves but through his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption (Hebrews 9:12). And by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified, according to the Scriptures (Hebrews 10:14). Now look, if you will, at another way as well in which the priest is crowned with the glory of Christ. Christ himself has cried out to us plainly, saying: ‘For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.’ (John 5:22–23) Again, this saying, spoken through the voice of a saint, stands in the sacred writings: ‘There is one Lawgiver and Judge.’ (James 4:12) And the inspired David also sings that ‘God is Judge.’ (Psalm 50:6; Psalm 75:7) Assigning this splendid dignity of judging to those of priestly blood, the lawgiver speaks in this way in Deuteronomy: ‘If a matter for judgment is too hard for you, between one kind of bloodshed and another, between one lawsuit and another, between one injury and another, between one dispute and another, matters for judgment in your cities, then you shall rise and go up to the place which the Lord your God chooses, and you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who is in office in those days; and they shall search the matter out and declare the judgment to you. And you shall act according to the matter which they declare to you from the place which the Lord your God chooses, and you shall take care to do all that is laid down for you. You shall act according to the law and according to the judgment that they tell you. You shall not turn aside from the word that they declare to you, to the right or to the left. And the man who acts… (Deuteronomy 17:8–12)

choices.why: δώσεις ἀργύριον ἐπί rendered 'spend the silver on'.
Cyril has εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, rendered 'the Holy of Holies' as he wrote it.
τὸ ἐπὶ τῷδε λαμπρὸν ἀξίωμα rendered 'this splendid dignity of judging', since τῷδε points back to the judging just described.
ὧδέ πη rendered 'in this way' (not 'something like this'), because the quotation is exact.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: Section opens mid-quotation (Deuteronomy 14:24, begun in section 19) and mid-turn; the quotation closes after 14:27. ἀποδώσῃ αὐτὰ ἀργυρίου ('give them back for silver') rendered 'sell them for silver'; δώσεις ἀργύριον ἐπί rendered 'spend the silver on'. Isaiah 26:7 matches the LXX word for word (ὁδὸς εὐσεβῶν εὐθεῖα ἐγένετο, καὶ παρεσκευασμένη ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν εὐσεβῶν). 'In a way that is at odds with the law': ἀπᾴδοντος τοῦ νόμου does not agree in gender with χειρός; I take it loosely with the offering or the offerer ('out of tune with the law'), not as a genitive absolute ('the law disagreeing'). Hebrews 9:12 reads εἰς τὰ ἅγια; Cyril has εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, rendered 'the Holy of Holies' as he wrote it. 'Through the voice of a saint' (δι' ἁγίου φωνῆς) introduces James 4:12 without naming James. 'God is Judge' (Θεὸς κριτής ἐστι): the exact phrase ὅτι ὁ θεὸς κριτής ἐστιν occurs in LXX Psalm 49:6 (English Psalm 50:6) and LXX Psalm 74:8 (English Psalm 75:7); both are cited because the words fit either. The long Greek period (genitive absolutes for Christ, James and David, then 'the lawgiver… says') is broken into several English sentences; the lawgiver here may be God or Moses speaking for God, so it is left lower-case outside the James quotation. Deuteronomy 17:8: αἷμα αἵματος, κρίσις κρίσεως, ἁφὴ ἁφῆς, ἀντιλογία ἀντιλογίας rendered 'between one case of blood and another…' (the LXX keeps the Hebrew idiom for distinguishing cases of homicide, rights, bodily injury or infection, and disputes); ἁφή kept as 'stroke' rather than narrowed to 'leprosy'. The printed text truncates 'the place which the Lord your God chooses ἐκεῖ' (the LXX adds ἐπικληθῆναι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ); ἐκεῖ rendered with 'go up there'. 'The judge who is in office in those days': 'in office' renders ὃς ἂν γένηται ('who may be'). Section ends mid-sentence in Deuteronomy 17:12 (καὶ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἐὰν ποιήσῃ); quotation left open. Review: in 17:8 the stray ἐκεῖ after ἐκλέξηται (the truncated ἐπικληθῆναι clause) is left untranslated rather than moved to 'go up there'. τὸ ἐπὶ τῷδε λαμπρὸν ἀξίωμα rendered 'this splendid dignity of judging', since τῷδε points back to the judging just described. ὧδέ πη rendered 'in this way' (not 'something like this'), because the quotation is exact. αἷμα αἵματος / κρίσις κρίσεως / ἁφὴ ἁφῆς rendered 'one kind of bloodshed / lawsuit / injury and another'; 'stroke' dropped as misleading in modern English.

review.method: translate from the Greek, then a separate clause-by-clause review against the Greek
changes: 'makes the hard roads very easy to travel' -> 'makes rough roads quite passable' (εὖ μάλα modifies the making, not ease)
James 4:12 frame: 'the sacred writings declare' -> 'this saying… stands in the sacred writings' (κείμενον)
ὧδέ πη: 'something like this' -> 'in this way'; 'dignity' clarified as 'dignity of judging'
Deut 17:8: 'case of blood / judgment / stroke' -> 'bloodshed / lawsuit / injury'; untranslatable stray ἐκεῖ dropped from 'go up there'; 'inquire' -> 'search the matter out'
Deut 17:11: fronted 'According to the law… you shall act' put in natural order
Inline citation for the Deuteronomy 14 quotation (begun in section 19) widened from 14:24–27 to 14:22–27 so the opening verses carry a reference in the reading text
assembly_edits: book-wide consistency: outer quotation marks ‘ ’, lower-case pronouns for God, US spelling, σκηνή = 'tent'
reader-facing translator_notes: row-join and review-history sentences removed; full note kept in apparatus
